content:
Client onboarding used to take my team 3 days. Now Viktor gets it ready for review in 40 minutes.

I run a social media and hiring agency, and after 15+ years in recruitment, I’ve learned that onboarding matters more than most teams think.

It’s one of the first moments a new client asks themselves: “Did I make the right choice?”
Our onboarding has four core steps.

Before viktor.com, every step depended on someone finding time to move it forward.

Now, when a new client pays, I tag Viktor in our channel and he starts working through the process.

My first instruction was basically: “Onboard our new client.”
The result was generic: a folder and a welcome email.

The quality of the workflow matters more than the cleverness of the prompt. 
That changed when I gave Viktor our four steps, our tone, and precise criteria for a completed handoff.

The difference:
→ Client folder: created when someone remembered → created in our shared drive when I tag him
→ Intake: written and sent manually → questionnaire + welcome email drafted
→ Content calendar: started from a blank page → first version prepared for review
→ Kickoff: arranged across multiple emails → kickoff email drafted and ready

Nothing goes to the client until a human approves it.

I hand Viktor the signup. My delivery team gets a prepared package to review.

A copilot helps you do the work. An AI employee moves it forward while your team focuses on judgment.
